chunks: From him, from Al-Mithammi, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Ahmarri, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'There is an open plot of land next to my house, enclosed by walls, whose owner I do not know; should I incorporate it into my house?' He said, 'Indeed, whoever takes a span of land without right will be brought on the Day of Resurrection with it around his neck from seven earths.'

key_terms.عَرْصَةً: an open plot of land or courtyard

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of taking land without knowing its owner in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling for incorporating an unknown, walled plot of land into one's property, warning that unjust appropriation carries a severe eschatological penalty. This narration emphasizes the gravity of *gharar* (uncertainty) in property rights, illustrating that even a small unjustly taken span of land will be physically manifested around the taker's neck on the Day of Judgment, extending from the seven earths.
